about: The texture space (public/shared/texture-space.js; docs/TEXTURE_SPACE.md): the named textures as locations among dimensions that name no instrument and no technique, so that every texture is an extension of the others and every point between them is one. The owner, 5 November 2026: "we need a layer of abstraction apart from instrument-specific textures but that can lead to them"; "to the extent possible, we want to avoid binding underlying musebot algorithms to specific instrumental techniques until they get close to the instrument". Each location's ranges the strings' textures' own, now said once; what a location does not read set so that a blend through it stays a texture.

texture-space.about: The texture space (public/shared/texture-space.js; docs/TEXTURE_SPACE.md): every texture a point among sixteen dimensions that name no instrument and no technique, each a share 0 to 1, each named texture a location of ranges [low, high] within them (the methods texture-<name> below). A pool draws its point within its location's ranges -- or a blend's, every range moved alike -- from its seed, each dimension evenly but those skewed here. Its two axes Huron's (1989): onset synchronization and semblant motion; the rest what the strings' ten textures had each done apart, said once.

pulseSkew.reason: a pool's pulse is its draw squared across its range, so most pools near its low end: a chord held more often than struck again, a cloud freer than pulsed (string-section.js, as the strings' chords and pizzicati were drawn)

semblanceSkew.reason: a pool's semblance is its draw's square root across its range, so most pools near its top: a counterpoint's lower parts imitating its top often (the owner, 3 October 2026: canons and fugues "more important"), as its imitation was drawn

glideSkew.reason: a pool's glide is its draw squared across its range, so most pools near its least: a note holding its pitch before it slides more often than sliding from its attack (the owner, 2 October 2026: bots "attack directly into glissandos in ways that I think should occur less often for their instruments")

figureTones.reason: a compound melody's walk over one to five of the harmony's tones, its compound a share across them: a trill's two, an Alberti bass's three, an arpeggio's more

divisions.reason: a part whose time is its own (its entry delayed, its pace drifting) is written on a lattice of its own: the beat divided from two to as many times as its player plays notes in it, the parts' shares spread evenly over this range from a drawn offset (no fixed set of tuplets: the owner, 2 October 2026, "the real limits are possible playing ... speed of the shortest notes")
